extracted.intended_audience: educators, curriculum designers, teachers, and students of educational philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for organizing school studies and methods grounded in an active/experimental conception of experience rather than passive sensationalism; guidance for integrating practical activities, laboratory methods, and the balance of naturalistic and humanistic studies in curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject pure sensationalism / object-lessons as sole pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not identify knowledge with a mere combination of sense-impressions or reduce instruction to isolated sensory exercises (object lessons). Sensationalism tends to isolate sensory qualities and treat sense-activity as an end in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipatterns: treating object lessons as the heart of instruction, making teaching a 'physical gymnastic' of sense organs. The text lists three serious defects of sensationalistic empiricism: (a) it is primarily critical/destructive rather than constructive for education; (b) direct impressions are limited in range and arrest development on a low plane; (c) it rests on a false psychology that neglects active, motor factors of experience. Use object lessons only as aids to thought, not as ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education should be constructive, not merely critical
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of education must build up new experience into intellectual habitudes that are as correct as possible from the start, rather than merely criticizing or dissolving existing beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid educational approaches that simply debunk traditional beliefs without providing a constructive plan for forming reliable intellectual habits. Teaching should aim to develop dispositions and capacities, not only to negate errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching must cultivate meaning and context, not isolated sensations
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning exists only with reference to a context; hence knowledge is responsiveness to meanings, not mere response to physical stimuli.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should situate sensory material within wider contexts and purposes so that students apprehend meanings, connections, and uses rather than isolated sensory qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete objects as aids to thought and progress to abstract symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete manipulatives (beans, counters, shoe pegs, etc.) can help realize numerical relations but must be used as aids to conceptual thinking; pupils must progress from concrete representations to abstract symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: prolonged reliance on physical tokens that arrests arithmetical understanding at the level of specific physical symbols. Encourage transition from concrete handling to conceptual operations and abstract notation as part of growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience is active and experimental — learning by doing and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience primarily consists of active relations between a person and their surroundings; knowing comes from doing, testing, and observing consequences under deliberate control (experimentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical implication: design learning as purposive experimentation (guided inquiry, controlled activities) so students learn connections between actions and outcomes. Examples: infants learn by handling; laboratory and controlled experiments extend this principle for scientific learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and design activities to intellectualize play and work
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectual studies should be an intellectualization of practical pursuits; practical activities can and should be shaped so as to cultivate intelligence rather than routine, trivial skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose school activities that make the intellectual content of contemporary practical pursuits explicit (e.g., household, agriculture, manufacturing with applied science). Activities should be selected and adapted to promote understanding and resourceful initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate the laboratory/experimental method early and meaningfully
rubrics_metrics.description: The laboratory is the condition under which doing becomes intellectually fruitful; laboratory methods teach that one must alter conditions and conduct controlled operations to obtain and test ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid treating the laboratory as an isolated or late-stage technical skill. Integrate experimentation into earlier studies so that pupils benefit fully from observational and experimental inquiry rather than merely acquiring technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: School must guide chance activities into deliberately selected educative activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Transport youth from environments of relatively chance activities into activities selected with reference to the guidance of learning, so that interactions produce meanings that serve as instruments for further learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the school environment to create situations where pupils' actions lead to measurable consequences and meaningful insights; deliberately arrange conditions to form intellectual dispositions rather than leaving development to whim or accidental experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use inquiry/discovery methods for material suited to investigation; reserve scholastic methods for fixed authoritative material
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholastic (textbook/authority-focused) methods are appropriate when the material is authoritative and received; where the material is an object of discovery or where nature/society is to be investigated, methods should emphasize inquiry, discovery, and invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antipattern: applying scholastic/interpretive methods (definition, exposition, dialectic) to subjects better learned through investigation. In such subjects prioritize methods that teach students to find out for themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance naturalistic and humanistic studies; relate science to human ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Naturalistic (scientific) studies are indispensable and should be pursued, but their purpose should be related to humanistic and ideal ends — science serves human interests and should support the aims of human life and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curriculum planning should avoid rigid division between nature and man; present natural studies as meaningful in the service of human ends and incorporate humanistic reflection alongside scientific instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject dualistic or purely mechanical philosophies that separate mind and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid educational outlooks grounded in philosophies that sharply divide mind and matter or reduce human life to mere mechanical phenomena; such outlooks improperly narrow what science and education claim to explain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let a mechanical/quantitative conception of science drive out qualitative, teleological, or human-centered aspects of education. Teach science as technique and method while acknowledging its limits and its role in human purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend and alter sense-perception through instruments and controlled operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific method involves altering and extending the data of sense-perception (e.g., through telescope, microscope, experimental devices); general concepts (mathematics) are implements for conducting and interpreting experimental inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instrumentation and designed experiments to broaden perceptual data and enable hypothesis formation and testing. Teach concepts as tools for instituting, conducting, and interpreting experiments rather than as self-sufficient sources of knowledge.
